title: Option strategies II: volatility plays
objectives: Know when to use a short volatility view.
body_md:
## Long straddle

Buy a call and a put at the **same strike and expiry**. Profits from a **large move** either way.

Example: K = 100, call 6 + put 5 = cost 11. **Breakevens: 89 and 111.** Max loss 11 at 100.

## Long strangle

Buy an OTM call and an OTM put. Cheaper than a straddle but needs a bigger move.

## Short straddle / strangle

Sell both. Profits if the price **stays range-bound**; risk is **unlimited**. Needs margin and strict risk limits.

## Butterfly and condor

Limited-risk range strategies using four options; they profit if the price stays near the middle.

## Choosing

| View | Strategy |
|---|---|
| Big move, direction unknown | Long straddle or strangle |
| Quiet market | Short straddle (high risk), iron condor (limited risk) |
| Volatility expected to fall | Short vega positions |

> **Exam tip:** Calculate straddle breakevens as K ± total premium.
example: Before results a trader expects a big move. Buying a 500 straddle for 40 profits if the stock goes below 460 or above 540.

A straddle needs a big enough move to beat the premium.
